RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-woman panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panels skew in all directions for mundane reasons — who was available, which departments or committees were represented. Raising it signals you're inferring bias from identity rather than from conduct, which weakens your credibility on the stronger points.

Your stronger points are concrete: the unanswered request for written reasons (most public universities owe this, often within a set deadline) and the apparent mismatch with advertised criteria. Push those. Escalate to the HR director or registrar in writing, cite the original job advert's stated requirements, and ask how each was scored.

Also stay open to the real possibility that she interviewed better or the department genuinely wanted industry links.
